assumptions: Metareasoning machinery consumes finite computational resources.
Partitioning problems require explicit resource distribution between planning and execution phases.
definition.falsification: Performance remains constant regardless of the ratio of resources allocated to planning versus execution, suggesting the partition problem does not impact output.
definition.statement: Rational agents bounded by metareasoning partition problems exhibit performance decay when the allocation between planning and execution is static, challenging the assumption of optimal unbounded reasoning in intelligent systems.
definition.uncertainty: The degree to which static allocation strategies fail across diverse, non-trivial problem sets remains empirically unverified in this context.

definition.method: Execute a resource-allocation simulation where planning overhead is varied. Measure solution accuracy against execution time and planning allocation ratio.
definition.stop: Completion of trials across all allocations.
definition.success: Accuracy significantly deviates when planning allocation is extreme (e.g., 0.1 or 0.9).

definition.cost: Minimal computational overhead for protocol execution.
definition.reason: The collected sources provide sufficient theoretical basis to begin formal experimental validation of the metareasoning partition assumption.
definition.stop_condition: Failure to demonstrate statistically significant variance in performance across allocation ratios.
definition.uncertainty: Whether empirical results from simple simulations generalize to complex cognitive architectures.

proposal.summary: This cycle formalizes the synthesis of architectural assumptions regarding metareasoning constraints into an testable hypothesis. By challenging the assumption of unbounded reasoning efficiency, we advance the investigation of reasoning blind spots within cognitive agent architectures.
proposal.title: Synthesis of Foundational Reasoning Constraints
